title: Equipotential Lines and Surfaces
notes: **Equipotential surface:** a surface on which the electric potential is the same at every point. No work is done moving a charge along it.
**Relation to field lines:** equipotential surfaces are always perpendicular to electric field lines.
**Point charge:** concentric spheres centred on the charge. Closer spheres mean stronger field because $\Delta V/\Delta r$ is larger.
**Uniform field:** parallel planes perpendicular to the field direction. Equal spacing means uniform field strength.
**Conductors:** the surface of a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium is an equipotential. The electric field just outside is perpendicular to the surface.
